concepts.title: Structure of Amines
concepts.definition: Amines feature a trivalent nitrogen atom with a lone pair, adopting a pyramidal geometry through sp3 hybridization.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, the presence of a lone pair on nitrogen reduces the bond angle from the ideal tetrahedral value.
question_patterns: describe the hybridization of nitrogen in amines
what is the geometry of a trimethylamine molecule
explain why the C-N-C bond angle in amines is less than 109.5 degrees
identify the shape of the ammonia derivative where H is replaced by alkyl groups

solution_steps.explain: The nitrogen atom in amines uses four sp3 hybrid orbitals, one of which contains a lone pair.
Due to three bonding pairs and one lone pair, the molecular geometry is pyramidal.

concepts.title: Classification of Amines
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, Amines are categorized as primary, secondary, or tertiary using the number of organic groups substituted for hydrogen in ammonia.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, the degree of an amine varies with the nitrogen's substitution level, not the carbon's.
question_patterns: classify the following as primary, secondary or tertiary amines
how many hydrogen atoms are replaced in a secondary amine
distinguish between simple and mixed amines
what defines a quaternary ammonium salt

solution_steps.explain: Count how many carbon-based groups are directly attached to the nitrogen atom.
1 group is primary (1°), 2 groups are secondary (2°), and 3 groups are tertiary (3°).

concepts.title: Ascent of Amine Series via Nitriles
concepts.definition: A synthetic method where nitriles are reduced to primary amines, resulting in a chain extension by one carbon atom.
concepts.key_idea: Reducing a nitrile group adds exactly one carbon to the parent alkyl chain.
question_patterns: calculate the number of carbons in the amine formed from a nitrile
how many carbons will the product have if ethyl chloride is converted to an amine via cyanide
find the carbon count of the amine produced by reducing propanenitrile
determine the length of the carbon chain in the resulting alkanamine

solution_steps.explain: The total carbons in the nitrile include the alkyl part and the CN carbon.

concepts.title: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
concepts.definition: The conversion of an amide into a primary amine with one less carbon atom by reaction with bromine and sodium hydroxide.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, the amide's carbonyl carbon is lost as carbonate, shortening the chain.
question_patterns: calculate the number of carbons in the amine formed by Hoffmann degradation
how many carbons are in the amide required to produce propanamine
find the carbon count of the product when butanamide reacts with Br2/KOH
determine the chain length reduction in Hoffmann bromamide reaction

solution_steps.explain: The amine formed contains one carbon less than the starting amide.

concepts.title: Boiling Point Trends in Amines
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the relative boiling points of isomeric amines determined by the extent of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
concepts.key_idea: Primary amines have more N-H bonds for hydrogen bonding than secondary, while tertiary have none.
question_patterns: arrange isomeric amines in increasing order of boiling points
why do primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines
compare the boiling points of n-butylamine and diethylamine
explain the effect of hydrogen bonding on amine volatility

solution_steps.explain: Primary amines have 2 N-H bonds, secondary have 1, and tertiary have 0.
More N-H bonds lead to stronger intermolecular association and higher boiling points.

concepts.title: Basicity of Amines (pKb)
concepts.definition: The measure of an amine's strength as a base, where lower pKb values indicate stronger basicity.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Aliphatic amines are indeed stronger bases than ammonia, while aromatic amines are weaker.
question_patterns: arrange the following amines in decreasing order of basic strength
compare the pKb values of ammonia and methanamine
why is aniline a weaker base than ammonia
explain the effect of electron-releasing groups on amine basicity

solution_steps.explain: Alkyl groups (+I) increase electron density on nitrogen, increasing basicity.
In arylamines, the lone pair is delocalized into the ring, decreasing basicity.

concepts.title: Carbylamine Reaction
concepts.definition: A chemical test specific to primary amines which produces foul-smelling isocyanides upon heating with both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both chloroform and KOH.
concepts.key_idea: Only primary amines (aliphatic or aromatic) give a positive isocyanide test.
question_patterns: how do you test for a primary amine
what is the product of the carbylamine reaction
identify the foul-smelling substance formed from aniline and chloroform
can secondary amines undergo the isocyanide test

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the starting material is a primary amine (R-NH2).
The reaction produces an isocyanide (carbylamine) characterized by a pungent odor.

concepts.title: Hinsberg Test
concepts.definition: A method to distinguish 1°, 2°, and 3° amines using benzenesulphonyl chloride based on the solubility of the product in alkali.
concepts.key_idea: 1° amines form alkali-soluble products; 2° form alkali-insoluble products; 3° do not react.
question_patterns: how to distinguish between ethylamine and diethylamine
what is Hinsberg's reagent
why is the product of a primary amine and Hinsberg reagent soluble in NaOH
describe the reaction of tertiary amines with benzenesulphonyl chloride

solution_steps.explain: Primary and secondary amines form sulphonamides; tertiary amines do not react.
The 1° amine product has an acidic H on nitrogen and dissolves; the 2° amine product lacks this H and is insoluble.

concepts.title: Diazotisation
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the reaction of primary aromatic amines with nitrous acid at 273-278 K to produce arenediazonium salts.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Low temperature is critical to prevent the diazonium's decomposition salt.
question_patterns: how is benzenediazonium chloride prepared
what are the reagents for diazotisation
why must diazotisation be carried out at 0-5 degrees Celsius
define the process of converting aniline to a diazonium salt

solution_steps.explain: NaNO2 reacts with HCl in situ to form HNO2.
The aromatic amine reacts with HNO2 at 273-278 K to form the stable arenediazonium cation.

concepts.title: Sandmeyer Reaction
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, the diazonium's substitution group in an aryl diazonium salt with Cl, Br, or CN using copper(I) salts.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Copper(I) ions catalyze the replacement of nitrogen by nucleophiles.
question_patterns: convert benzenediazonium chloride to chlorobenzene
what is the catalyst in the Sandmeyer reaction
how to introduce a cyano group into a benzene ring using diazonium salts
compare Sandmeyer and Gattermann reactions

solution_steps.explain: Use Cu2Cl2 for chloro, Cu2Br2 for bromo, or CuCN for cyano substitution.
The diazonium group leaves as N2 gas, and the nucleophile attaches to the ring.

concepts.title: Azo Coupling Reaction
concepts.definition: An electrophilic substitution reaction where a diazonium cation reacts with an activated aromatic ring to form a colored azo compound.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the resulting -N=N- linkage creates an extended conjugated system, typically a dye.
question_patterns: how is p-hydroxyazobenzene formed
describe the reaction between benzenediazonium chloride and phenol
what are azo dyes
identify the product of coupling between aniline and a diazonium salt

solution_steps.explain: The partner must be an electron-rich aromatic compound like phenol or aniline.
The diazonium nitrogen attacks the para position of the partner to form the N=N bridge.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Identify the amide which gives {amine_name} by Hoffmann bromamide reaction.

solution_template.explain: In Hoffmann degradation, the amide has one more carbon than the resulting amine.
